observations: The seventh site the architect asked about: two unfenced writes exist, both traced here, and neither produces the harm the fence exists to stop. A read-only audit of every function reachable from `passes.run` or `roleMoves.run`, for an await followed by a write to module state without re-reading `live()`/`owns()`/`stillHolds()`, found exactly two. (a) `registerSession`'s `.then` (envoy.ts:1622-1623) stamps `registeredFor`/`registeredAt` with no fence, so a pass abandoned for session S1 whose registration answers late can stamp S1 after a newer pass recorded S2. The stamp is honest - that registration really was accepted at the listener - and the only effect is that the backstop then treats S2 as unregistered and posts one extra registration outside the queues, which is the safe direction. (b) `settleEndedHolds`'s restore loop (envoy.ts:2299-2301) writes `pendingHandBacks`/`abandonedHolds` before its `live()` re-read at :2305, deliberately, because the holds whose hand-back failed are in neither map while the loop runs and dropping them would leak them (the comment at :2274-2278 says so). A move abandoned mid-hand-back can therefore restore an entry a newer claim cleared at :1939-1942. I traced every path out of that resurrection: an entry restored under the host's own id makes the next pass take the restore branch at :2281-2286 (one redundant soft claim of a role the session already holds, and possibly the 'notices stay closed' warning), and one restored under a session the host left is handed back to a listener that no longer names that session for the role, so the listener drops nothing. Neither reaches the harm class of the three findings already fixed - a role taken from the claim that replaced the abandoned move - so this is recorded rather than failed. It is the one site where a future change to `wanted` or to a caller could make the clobber matter, and it is the first place to look if a fourth such finding appears.
